restaurants.name: Restaurante O Barradas
restaurants.knownFor: Traditional Algarvian cooking in an unchanged setting. The cataplana is legendary.
restaurants.insiderTip: Ask for a table in the back garden. The owner still runs the grill himself most evenings.

restaurants.name: A Eira do Mel
restaurants.knownFor: Mountain cuisine done right. The frango piri-piri is cooked over charcoal.
whatToSkip: Fish dishes — go mountain or go home
restaurants.insiderTip: Come hungry. Portions are huge and meant to share family-style.

restaurants.name: Casa do Polvo Tasquinha
restaurants.knownFor: The octopus capital of Portugal. Every dish features polvo.
restaurants.insiderTip: Walk around the village before lunch — Santa Luzia is the real thing, not a tourist setup.

restaurants.name: Dois Irmãos
restaurants.knownFor: Fresh catches at working-town prices. The fish is swimming in the morning.
restaurants.insiderTip: Sit on the terrace facing the market. Go early for Saturday lunch when the market is buzzing.

restaurants.name: A Tasca do Kiko
restaurants.knownFor: Tiny tasca where locals eat. No menu — you eat what's cooking.
restaurants.insiderTip: Go at lunch, sit at the counter, and let Kiko choose for you. Trust the process.

restaurants.name: Tasca do Zé
restaurants.knownFor: Surfer-friendly tasca with homestyle cooking and cold beer.
restaurants.insiderTip: The portions are massive. One main dish is enough for most people.

restaurants.name: Noelia & Jerónimo
restaurants.knownFor: Michelin-starred tasting menus with Ria Formosa views.
whatToSkip: À la carte — the tasting menu is the experience
restaurants.insiderTip: Book the sunset seating. The view over the salt flats during golden hour is unforgettable.

restaurants.name: Vila Joya
restaurants.knownFor: Two Michelin stars and ocean views. The Algarve's finest dining.
whatToSkip: Nothing — let them guide the experience
restaurants.insiderTip: Book weeks in advance, especially for Friday/Saturday. Dress smart casual.

restaurants.name: Café Calcinha
restaurants.knownFor: The market's best pastel de nata and strong coffee.
restaurants.insiderTip: Go Saturday morning when the market is at full swing. The custard tarts fly out of the oven.

restaurants.name: Casa Velha
restaurants.knownFor: Homestyle petiscos and local wine in a cozy setting.
restaurants.insiderTip: The back room is quieter. Order several petiscos to share instead of mains.

restaurants.name: Mirandus
restaurants.knownFor: Sunset cocktails with the best cliff views in the Algarve.
whatToSkip: Heavy mains — come for views and drinks
restaurants.insiderTip: Book a terrace table for sunset (1.5 hours before). Arrive early for photos without crowds.

restaurants.name: Maria's Beach Bar
restaurants.knownFor: Feet-in-the-sand dining with grilled fish and cold wine.
whatToSkip: Anything complicated — stick to simple grilled dishes
restaurants.insiderTip: The best table is the one furthest from the path, right on the sand.
